title: PARTICIPLES
notes:
✓ Participle → a verb form that can function as part of a verb phrase or as an adjective.

◆ TWO MAIN TYPES
✓ Present participle → verb + -ing.
✓ Past participle → usually the third form of the verb (V3).

✓ Present participle → running, studying, interesting.
✓ Past participle → broken, written, excited, finished.

⚠️ A participle is different from a finite verb because it does not normally show tense by itself.

title: PRESENT PARTICIPLES
notes:
✓ Present participle → the -ing form of a verb.

✓ work → working
✓ study → studying
✓ run → running
✓ write → writing

◆ MAIN USES
✓ Continuous tenses
✓ Participial phrases
✓ Adjectives

✓ She is studying. → part of a verb phrase.
✓ The crying baby needs attention. → adjective.
✓ Walking down the road, he saw his friend. → participial phrase.

title: PAST PARTICIPLES
notes:
✓ Past participle → usually the third form of a verb (V3).

✓ work → worked → worked
✓ write → wrote → written
✓ break → broke → broken
✓ see → saw → seen

◆ MAIN USES
✓ Perfect tenses
✓ Passive voice
✓ Adjectives
✓ Participial phrases

✓ She has finished. → perfect tense.
✓ The window was broken. → passive voice.
✓ He looked worried. → adjective.
✓ Shocked by the news, she left. → participial phrase.

title: PARTICIPLES IN CONTINUOUS TENSES
notes:
✓ The present participle (-ing) is used with forms of 'be' to make continuous tenses.

✓ Present continuous → She is reading.
✓ Past continuous → She was reading.
✓ Future continuous → She will be reading.

✓ Structure → be + present participle.

⚠️ The -ing form alone does not normally make a complete continuous verb.

❌ She reading a book.
✓ She is reading a book.

title: PARTICIPLES IN PERFECT TENSES
notes:
✓ The past participle is used with have/has/had to form perfect tenses.

✓ Present perfect → She has written the letter.
✓ Past perfect → She had written the letter.
✓ Future perfect → She will have written the letter.

✓ Structure → have/has/had + past participle.

⚠️ Use V3, not V2, after have/has/had.

❌ She has wrote the letter.
✓ She has written the letter.

title: PARTICIPLES IN PASSIVE VOICE
notes:
✓ The past participle is used with forms of 'be' to form passive constructions.

✓ The house was built in 1990.
✓ The letters are written every day.
✓ The work has been completed.

✓ Basic passive structure → be + past participle.

✓ Perfect passive → have + been + past participle.
✓ The work has been completed.

title: PARTICIPLES AS ADJECTIVES
notes:
✓ Participles can describe nouns like adjectives.

◆ -ING ADJECTIVES
✓ Usually describe the thing/person that causes a feeling or has an effect.
✓ The movie was boring.
✓ The lesson is interesting.

◆ -ED/V3 ADJECTIVES
✓ Usually describe the person or thing experiencing the feeling/result.
✓ I was bored.
✓ She was interested.

✓ Key idea →
BORING → causes the feeling.
BORED → experiences the feeling.

title: -ING VS -ED PARTICIPLE ADJECTIVES
notes:
✓ Interesting → causing interest.
✓ Interested → feeling interest.

✓ Boring → causing boredom.
✓ Bored → feeling boredom.

✓ Exciting → causing excitement.
✓ Excited → feeling excitement.

✓ Confusing → causing confusion.
✓ Confused → experiencing confusion.

✓ Frightening → causing fear.
✓ Frightened → experiencing fear.

✓ The teacher gave an interesting lesson.
✓ The students were interested in the lesson.

✓ Remember → -ING = cause; -ED = experience/result.

title: PARTICIPIAL PHRASES
notes:
✓ Participial phrase → a phrase beginning with a present or past participle that gives additional information about the subject.

◆ PRESENT PARTICIPLE PHRASE
✓ Walking to school, I met my friend.
✓ Looking out of the window, she saw the accident.

◆ PAST PARTICIPLE PHRASE
✓ Shocked by the news, he said nothing.
✓ Built in 1900, the house is very old.

✓ Participial phrases make sentences shorter and more concise.

title: REDUCED CLAUSES WITH PARTICIPLES
notes:
✓ Participles can reduce certain clauses when the subject is understood to be the same.

✓ Because she was tired, she went home.
→ Being tired, she went home.

✓ After he finished his work, he went home.
→ Having finished his work, he went home.

✓ Because he was shocked by the news, he left.
→ Shocked by the news, he left.

✓ The reduced form removes unnecessary words while keeping the meaning.

title: PERFECT PARTICIPLE
notes:
✓ Perfect participle → having + past participle (V3).

✓ Having finished the work, she went home.
✓ Having studied hard, he passed the exam.
✓ Having completed the project, they submitted it.

✓ It shows that one action happened before another action.

✓ Pattern → having + V3 + main clause.

✓ Having eaten dinner, we watched a movie.
→ First: ate dinner.
→ Second: watched a movie.

title: PASSIVE PERFECT PARTICIPLE
notes:
✓ Perfect participles can also be passive.

✓ Pattern → having been + past participle.

✓ Having been warned about the danger, they left immediately.
✓ Having been invited to the event, she decided to attend.

✓ Meaning → the participial action happened before the main action and was received by the subject.

title: PAST PARTICIPLE PHRASES
notes:
✓ Past participle phrases often express a passive meaning or a resulting condition.

✓ Written in English, the letter was easy to understand.
✓ Surrounded by mountains, the village is beautiful.
✓ Tired after the journey, they went to bed.

✓ Compare:
✓ Running down the street, he fell. → active idea.
✓ Exhausted by the journey, he rested. → passive/resulting state.

title: DANGLING PARTICIPLES
notes:
✓ A dangling participle occurs when the participial phrase does not logically describe the subject of the main clause.

❌ Walking to school, the rain started.
→ The sentence incorrectly suggests that the rain was walking.

✓ Walking to school, I got caught in the rain.

✓ The implied subject of the participial phrase should normally be the same as the subject of the main clause.

title: REGULAR & IRREGULAR PAST PARTICIPLES
notes:
✓ Regular verbs → past participle usually ends in -ed.

✓ work → worked → worked
✓ clean → cleaned → cleaned
✓ play → played → played

✓ Irregular verbs → past participles have different forms.

✓ go → went → gone
✓ write → wrote → written
✓ eat → ate → eaten
✓ take → took → taken
✓ break → broke → broken
✓ see → saw → seen
✓ speak → spoke → spoken

✓ Irregular past participles must be learned individually.

title: COMMON ERRORS
notes:
❌ She has went home.
✓ She has gone home.

❌ He is interesting in science.
✓ He is interested in science.

❌ The students were boring by the lesson.
✓ The students were bored by the lesson.

❌ Walking to school, the accident happened.
✓ Walking to school, I saw the accident.

❌ Having finish the work, he left.
✓ Having finished the work, he left.

❌ The letter was wrote yesterday.
✓ The letter was written yesterday.

✓ Check whether the participle is being used correctly as V3, -ing form, adjective, or part of a phrase.

title: EXAM GUIDE
notes:
◆ 1. Present participle → V-ing.
✓ running, studying, writing.

◆ 2. Past participle → V3.
✓ written, broken, finished.

◆ 3. Continuous → be + V-ing.
✓ is studying.

◆ 4. Perfect → have + V3.
✓ has studied.

◆ 5. Passive → be + V3.
✓ was written.

◆ 6. -ING adjective → usually causes a feeling.
✓ The movie is exciting.

◆ 7. -ED/V3 adjective → usually experiences a feeling/result.
✓ I am excited.

◆ 8. Participial phrase → V-ing/V3 + additional information.
✓ Feeling tired, she went home.

◆ 9. Perfect participle → having + V3.
✓ Having finished, he left.

◆ 10. Always check the subject of a participial phrase to avoid dangling constructions.

✓ Golden rule → Present participle = V-ing; past participle = V3; perfect participle = having + V3.
